generation.explanation: Completing the square turns x² + 6x into a perfect square minus a constant. Geometrically, x² is a square of side x, and 6x is a rectangle of width 6. Split that rectangle into two pieces of width 3, attach one to each side of the square, and you get an (x+3) by (x+3) square with a 3×3 corner missing. That missing piece has area 9, so x² + 6x = (x+3)² − 9.
